about.text: Toned milk is milk, usually from buffalo, whose fat is brought down to about 3 % by adding skim milk, skim milk powder and water, while the non-fat solids are restored to their original level. It was devised in India to stretch scarce milk and sell buffalo milk at a price near cow milk.

sources.text: Much of India’s packaged milk: its dairies handle about a fifth of its 239 Mt, about two thirds of that sold as milk, toned or double-toned the most of it.

facts.v: Toned: 3.0 % fat, 8.5 % solids-not-fat. Double-toned: 1.5 % fat, 9.0 % solids-not-fat (secondary sources; check the FSS Food Products Standards text, newer norms exist)
